children.title: Trump Threatens Jail for Reporter Who Won’t Reveal Iran Airman-Rescue Source
children.description_short: Trump threatened jail if a reporter withheld the source of an Iran airman-rescue story.
children.description_medium: Reuters reported that Trump said at a White House press conference on April 6, 2026, that he would demand the source behind a report about the rescue of an airman in Iran and threatened jail if the reporter refused to disclose it. The report documents a threat; it does not say the journalist was jailed or that the source was disclosed.
children.description_long: At a White House press conference on April 6, 2026, President Donald Trump said he would seek the source of reporting that an American airman had been rescued in Iran and threatened jail if the journalist refused to identify the source, according to Reuters. This card isolates those public remarks from the later subpoenas described in the original combined entry. Reuters’s account supports that Trump made the threat, but the material reviewed does not establish that the reporter was jailed, that a source was identified, or that a prosecution or court order followed. The reported threat concerned one reporter and a specific national-security story; it should not be presented as an actual imprisonment. The supplied record does not identify the journalist, establish the source of the rescue report, or describe subsequent legal proceedings against the reporter. The threatened action therefore remains a reported presidential statement, with potential implications for source confidentiality but no documented sanction in the material used for this draft. The separate June Justice Department subpoena episode belongs in its own card because the supplied reporting does not connect it to the airman-rescue disclosure.

The reviewed reporting does not establish that the subpoenas concerned that rescue disclosure, and the prior supplied account itself says the precise investigations were unclear. It supports a narrower account: DOJ sought reporter testimony and withdrew the subpoenas after the news organizations challenged them. The exact dates on which the subpoenas were issued and withdrawn are not established by the excerpt used here; June 23 is the report date.

title: Khamenei Rejects Trump’s Surrender Demand and Warns Against U.S. Intervention
description_short: Khamenei rejected Trump’s surrender demand and warned of damage if the U.S. entered the conflict.
description_medium: An Associated Press report published by PBS on June 18, 2025, said Ayatollah Ali Khamenei rejected President Donald Trump’s call for Iran’s unconditional surrender and warned that U.S. military involvement would cause “irreparable damage.” The report says Khamenei delivered the remarks in recorded video during Israeli strikes. This corrected draft omits the unsupported “gates of hell” and “severe and unrelenting” quotations.
description_long: On June 18, 2025, Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei rejected U.S. President Donald Trump’s demand for Iran’s unconditional surrender and warned that any U.S. military involvement would cause “irreparable damage,” according to an Associated Press report carried by PBS News. The report says Khamenei made the remarks in a recorded video aired by Iranian state television as Israeli strikes continued. It describes the address as Khamenei’s second public appearance since the strikes began and notes that Trump’s surrender demand came the previous day. This account corrects the frozen card’s June 15 date and narrows its claims to the remarks supported by the accessed report. The source does not support attributing “gates of hell” or a vow of “severe and unrelenting” revenge to Khamenei; those phrases are removed. Search results located “gates of hell” wording attributed to other Iranian figures, so that language is not reassigned to Khamenei. The reporting supports his rejection of the surrender demand and his conditional warning about U.S. military intervention. It does not establish the frozen card’s claims about proxy forces, global travel alerts, embassy closures, or a U.S. strike already having occurred before these June 18 remarks.
date_basis: Statement date in the AP/PBS report.

title: Supplied Account: Alleged Attorney Arrest After Alien Enemies Act Hearing
description_short: Internal draft of an unverified claim that an immigration attorney was arrested after court advocacy.
description_medium: The supplied entry alleges that ICE arrested a private immigration attorney in April 2025 shortly after she argued an Alien Enemies Act challenge, and that officials cited alleged foreign funding for her advocacy organization. description_long: This internal draft reflects only the supplied record’s account of an alleged April 2025 arrest of a private immigration attorney. The record says the attorney had appeared in federal court for clients challenging removals under the Alien Enemies Act and that ICE agents arrested her near the courthouse shortly afterward. It further says officials invoked alleged foreign funding for the attorney’s advocacy organization, while her lawyers called that rationale false and pretextual. The supplied text attributes objections to bar associations, the National Lawyers Guild and the American Immigration Lawyers Association. Those details remain claims from the frozen record; the search conducted for this repair did not independently verify them. That is a different person and event and does not substantiate or replace the alleged attorney arrest. The supplied record does not name the lawyer, court, clients, docket, arresting officers, or the specific bar statements, and it provides no source links or primary documents. The exact arrest date, stated legal basis, procedural outcome and any connection to administration officials remain unknown. This copy preserves the supplied allegation for internal review only; publication would require evidence tied to this specific attorney and event.
